title: Move the authored construction-site landmark into its own mini-game subpackage

buildVerdict.rawLine: PASS wechatgame: 203 files, launch=db://assets/scenes/Game.scene, boot=world-city, subpackages=[world-construction,world-city], AppID=wx6ac3f5090a6b99c5 (configured), libVersion=widelyUsed.

whyThisAssetWasFirst.claim: world-construction was the single largest removable block in the WeChat main package.
whyThisAssetWasFirst.evidence: One source file, cocos/assets/resources/art/construction/majadroid-construction-site.fbx (789,276 B), imported by Creator into a 43,142-triangle mesh. In the previous build that mesh alone was cocos/build/wechatgame/assets/resources/native/41/41c6d840-...@8fac0.bin = 4,376,316 B.
whyThisAssetWasFirst.independentCheck: The pre-change main package was measured directly from the built artifact rather than trusted from the WP0 audit: assets/resources totalled 4,731,829 B (4,621 KiB), matching wechat-bundle-map.json's 4,617 KB claim to within 0.1%.
whyThisAssetWasFirst.lazyLoadProof: The fbx uuid 41c6d840-10ea-4014-8347-113f26874377 appears in no .scene/.prefab/.json under cocos/assets - it is reachable only through the callback resources.load() call, i.e. it is genuinely lazy and safe to move out of the boot path.

changeSet.whyNotUnderResources: Creator does not support nested Asset Bundles and cocos/assets/resources is itself a bundle (bundleName=resources), so the asset had to leave that subtree entirely. A dedicated cocos/assets/bundles/ root was chosen because the remaining WP4 groups (shared-gameplay, endless, arena, cosmetics) are not art and do not belong under art/.

leftAlone.cocos/assets/resources/material.mtl: Orphan cc.Material (uuid 260eecc4-3375-4111-8739-17e20b232bc3), 225 B, referenced by neither the construction prefab nor assets/main. Kept in place so the resources bundle stays a valid, non-empty bundle; it is not part of this logical group and moving it would be unrelated churn.

code.change: Added getBundle(bundleName): AssetManager.Bundle | null - the resident bundle or null. Narrow accessor so a caller can address an asset inside an already-loaded bundle without standing up a second loader.
code.why: Reuses the existing service instead of adding a second loading mechanism, which the mandate forbids.

code.change: Added CONSTRUCTION_LANDMARK_BUNDLE / CONSTRUCTION_LANDMARK_ASSET constants; rewrote loadConstructionLandmark() to go through regionBundles.ensureLoaded() then bundle.load(); added failConstructionLandmark(); removed the now-unused `resources` import.
code.deliberatelyNotDone: The landmark was NOT added to REGION_ASSET_BUNDLES and NOT added to BOOT_BUNDLES. It is optional scenery that no cell waits on, and gating the opening cell on a 4.6 MB download would delay the first frame for every player. Failure still degrades to 'no landmark', exactly as before.

code.change: observeRegionArtAttempt() now derives the player-facing message from that attempt's own rejection instead of this.regionBundles.getLastFailure().
code.why: The service keeps one 'last failure' slot. With a second bundle able to be in flight, a world-construction failure could otherwise have been reported as the message for a world-city failure. This removes a cross-bundle coupling that this change would have introduced.

code.change: Added 6 checks: BUNDLE_ROOTS_ENUMERATED (walks cocos/assets for isBundle metas), NO_NESTED_BUNDLE_ROOTS, CONSTRUCTION_BUNDLE_META_EXISTS, CONSTRUCTION_BUNDLE_IS_SUBPACKAGE, CONSTRUCTION_BUNDLE_OWNS_ITS_ASSET, CONSTRUCTION_BUNDLE_NOT_IN_BOOT, CONSTRUCTION_LOADER_USES_BUNDLE (also asserts no resources.load remains).
code.why: Turns this change into an enforced contract rather than a claim. All 28 checks in the file pass.

packageGate.method: Byte-exact recursive sum of cocos/build/wechatgame; main = total minus everything under subpackages/. Not a directory estimate.
packageGate.internalTargetCaveat: 3482 KiB is the project's own headroom target (85% of the official limit), NOT a WeChat threshold.

delta.note: Total also fell because the asset is packed differently as a subpackage than as part of the resources bundle.

packageGate.verdict: BLOCKED - main is still 2.60x the official 4,096 KiB limit. This step is real progress (-32.0% of main), not a pass.

mainCompositionAfter.decisiveFinding: The engine bundle alone (cocos-js, 4,051.2 KiB) is 98.9% of the entire 4,096 KiB main-package budget. Main cannot reach 4 MB by moving assets no matter how many are moved; only engine-level options (separateEngine, engine module cropping, wasmSubpackage) can cross it. This confirms B1 empirically and is an owner decision, not a WP4 task.

assetLeftMain.check: grep -rl for both the raw uuid 41c6d840 and its compressed form 41xthAEOpAFINHET8mh0N3 across cocos/build/wechatgame/assets/main/

gameJson.note: Formal subpackage declaration produced by Creator's own bundle config. game.json was NOT hand-edited.

runtimeGate.whyTwoPlatforms: The mini-game has no QA probe: GameManager.installQABridgeIfRequested() gates on globalThis.location.search, which only exists in a browser. So the mini-game run proves the *packaging* (subpackage downloads, game boots and plays) and the web-mobile run proves the *code path* (the landmark actually loads from its own bundle and installs).

minigame.method: WeChat DevTools Stable 2.01.2510290 simulator, recompiled (工具 -> 编译) to load the new build, then OS-level input via .scratch/wechat-click-shot.ps1.
verified: cold start reaches Home with the world rendered (no black screen, no boot-bundle retry overlay)
the file tree shows the rebuilt project including subpackages/
gameplay runs: coins 72, LV.1 级黑洞, 质量150kg, region 卧室杂物区, roads/trees/vehicles/HUD all present
minigame.console: 调试器 badge 2 errors / 3 warnings, and the visible Console line is the DevTools-internal devtools_profile_parser message. This is the same state as the WP3c baseline, which was accepted as having no game-side error. The dock cannot be enlarged enough to enumerate every row, so this is NOT a row-by-row proof - it is stated as a limitation.
minigame.notVerifiable: The landmark's own loadState/visible cannot be read on the mini-game target, because there is no QA probe there.

webMobile.method: GameManager.onLoad() calls initWorld() -> loadConstructionLandmark(), so the bundle download starts at boot. The driver then clicks Home -> Mode Select -> Endless Ready -> Start using the published layout anchors and reads the read-only QA bridge.
webMobile.bundleDownload: 8 responses matching world-construction (config.json, index.js, import/*, native/*), all HTTP 200.
webMobile.whyVisibleIsFalseAtHome: While gameState is HOME the streamer has 8 cells loaded (the neighbours of 0:0) but not 0:0 itself, and installConstructionLandmarkInOpeningCell() attaches to the 0:0 cell. Once gameplay starts, activeCellCount becomes 9 including 0:0 and visible flips to true. This is pre-existing behaviour: git diff -U0 shows installConstructionLandmarkInOpeningCell() and hasConstructionLandmark() are untouched by this change - only the call site moved.

runtimeGate.verdict: PASS for this step - the landmark loads from the new bundle and installs in the opening cell; boot, Home, Mode Select, Endless Ready and Endless Start all work on both targets.

regression.command: npm run test:full  (= test:cocos + test:contracts + test:authoring)
regression.note: grep for FAIL returns 6 hits, but all six are [PASS] lines whose text contains the word (BOOT_FAILURE_HAS_RETRY, SERVICE_RETRIES_THEN_FAILS, SERVICE_FAILED_IS_TERMINAL, ...). An explicit grep for the [FAIL] token returns 0.

incident.what: Running `git rm` inside this repo caused the tool to SIGTERM the command (empty output, exit 1), and the workspace rollback then sent the ENTIRE cocos/assets tree (439 files) to the Windows Recycle Bin, per-file and bottom-up, leaving a 0-byte .git/index.lock behind.
incident.reproduced: Twice, at 01:54 and 02:02 local; the second batch contained exactly the same 435 entries.
incident.notCausedByGit: git rm itself never executed - git status showed no staged deletion and index.lock was still held. rmdir never executed either. The recycle window contained exactly 435 entries, all under cocos/assets, spanning 17:54:37-17:54:58 UTC.
incident.sideEffect: The recycle routine rewrote file contents in text mode, so the restored worktree files are now LF while core.autocrlf=true. Git reports every untouched file as unmodified, so this is benign; `git checkout --` must NOT be used to 'fix' it because that would discard uncommitted edits.
incident.recovery: Full. All 439 files restored by copying (not moving) the $R payloads back - .scratch/restore_assets.py. Note the $R payload for the top-level directory is only a partial tree, so every entry must be restored, not just the directory. Verified: 439 files = 439 files, git status deletions = 0, git diff --check clean, typecheck PASS.
incident.rule: Never use `git rm` or `rmdir` in this repo; delete with plain `rm` or Python. After any SIGTERM'd command, check for and remove .git/index.lock.

artifacts.note: cocos/docs/evidence/v2/platform/mini-build-report.json is overwritten by every build:* run. It was backed up to .scratch/v2-platform-backup/ before this build and restored from that backup afterwards with cp (no git write command was used), so the committed baseline is unchanged.

whatThisRunProves: A real Cocos build produces a second formal WeChat subpackage, declared in game.json by Creator's own bundle config - not by hand-editing build output.
The heaviest asset in the project no longer appears anywhere in the main package (0 uuid hits in assets/main).
The main package fell from 15,624 KiB to 10,629.3 KiB, measured byte-exactly on the built artifact.
The engine bundle alone is 98.9% of the official main-package budget, so B1 cannot be solved by asset moves.
Typecheck passes and the region-bundle contract now enforces the new bundle's shape.
whatThisRunDoesNotProve: That the construction landmark still renders at runtime - the runtime gate for this step has not been run yet.
That the subpackage downloads correctly on a real device or in the WeChat DevTools simulator with the download path exercised.
That main can reach the 4 MB limit: it cannot, without engine-level changes (owner decision).
That the remaining WP4 groups (shared-gameplay, endless, arena, cosmetics) will behave the same way - each needs its own build/size/runtime/regression cycle.
nextWork: Run the runtime gate for this step: cold start, Home, Mode Select, Endless Ready/Start, world-opening load, Cell streaming, and confirm the construction landmark still installs in the opening cell from the new bundle.

Then continue WP4 in audit-contribution order: shared-gameplay (3,205 KiB) -> endless (248 KiB) -> arena -> cosmetics. The last two are reserved-empty in wechat-bundle-map.json because neither has any exclusive asset.
Owner decisions still outstanding: separateEngine, main-as-subpackage, engine cropping, skybox, stripping release debug code, and B12 (updateHighScore semantics).
